transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
A powerful storm developing along the east coast is expected to disrupt Thanksgiving
travel.
Heavy rain and strong winds could slow drivers and delay flights across parts of the Mid-Atlantic
and northeast.
In New York City, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first
time in its 100-year history.
NPR's Steve Kastenbaum reports.
The storm is forecast to bring heavy rains and strong wind gusts to New York and the
surrounding region tomorrow.
In a written statement, Macy's officials said the safety of participants and spectators
is their top priority, and after consultations with city agencies, they decided to move this
year's celebration.
Huge crowds had already taken part in an annual pre-parade event, watching the inflation of
the giant balloons.
A record 100 inflatables were set to make their way along the parade route.
They now expect to kick off the Thanksgiving Day Parade Saturday morning at 8.30.
Steve Kastenbaum, NPR News in New York.
The Trump administration has posted emails and other files on the U.S. Agency for International
Development website to try to discredit the Biden administration's agenda there.
NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports the documents are related to the organization's efforts
to counter disinformation.
One of the programmers that Elon Musk brought to Washington to dismantle USAID says, "You
can now read internal memos showing how the agency operated.
The so-called USAID files detail the Biden administration's contacts with social media
companies.
At the time, it was U.S. policy to push back on disinformation from Russia, China and others.
The Trump administration officials say USAID was weaponized to advance a radical agenda.
The State Department says it welcomed the release of the documents and referred questions
to the Office of Management and Budget, which oversees what's left of USAID.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
The Army has destroyed nearly five tons of a hazardous chemical that was stockpiled at
a facility in southeastern Iowa.
Tom Barton from Iowa Public Radio reports the EPA hasn't detected any lead in the air.
State and federal officials say early reports indicate the blast went as planned.
Army Major General Eric Shirley called it better than expected.
I believe absolutely that we reduced as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible
to risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities
throughout Iowa.
Federal groups had warned that toxic lead deaths could spread across parts of rural
Iowa and northeastern Missouri.
The EPA, local health officials and local universities continue to monitor air quality
and test soil and water samples.
For NPR News, I'm Tom Barton in Des Moines.
This is NPR News in Washington.
With food and travel costs climbing, there's not much that has gotten cheaper this Thanksgiving.
Just unless your family is among those who bring marijuana to the party, NPR's Marissa
J. Lang reports.
You know that moment before or after the big meal when the cousins take a walk outside
and come back a little happy, hungry, maybe a little stoned?
For Americans like Kelly Vinton, it's a Thanksgiving staple.
We just smoke a joint and we get nice and high and get some munchies and get ready for
dinner.
At the cost of that big holiday meal, cannabis prices have dropped.
That's because there's an oversupply of plant product.
And economist Bo Whitney says an industry culture that draws customers in with discounts.
The operators are getting crushed because there's all this oversupply in the market.
Retailers hope that Green Wednesday, as the lead up to Thanksgiving is known, will boost
revenue thanks to those who want to bring a little something extra to the family feast.
Marissa J. Lang, NPR News, Baltimore.
The Federal Communications Commission has cleared SpaceX to put up to a million satellites
into orbit to serve as data centers.
The satellites would process data in space for artificial intelligence systems used on
Earth.
SpaceX says it plans to power the onboard computers with solar energy.
It's the first time the FCC has authorized a network of data centers in space under the
license the company has until November of 2033 to begin deploying the satellites.
This is NPR.
This week on Here and Now Anytime, practicing gratitude isn't just for Thanksgiving.
The person who experiences the feeling of gratitude can do a lot of things for both
their mental health and their physical health.
Also batch cocktails and mocktails for holiday hosting.
It's this week on Here and Now Anytime, listen on the NPR app or anywhere you listen to podcasts.

topics.text: Powerful East Coast storm threatens Thanksgiving travel delays across Mid-Atlantic and Northeast
Macy's postpones Thanksgiving Day Parade for first time in 100-year history due to storm
Trump administration posts USAID files online to discredit Biden-era disinformation efforts
Army destroys nearly five tons of hazardous chemical at southeastern Iowa facility, no lead detected
Cannabis prices drop ahead of Thanksgiving as oversupply hits the market
FCC clears SpaceX to launch up to a million satellites serving as orbital data centers
